title: Fragment arbitration and tool-decline protocol - acceptance criteria
creator: Priya Shah
background: Customers are integrating Redwood streaming responses with downstream tool gateways (third-party APIs and internal service adapters). We observed two recurring failure modes in recent pilot integrations: (1) streamed structured fragments that never reach a consistent commit point, and (2) tool endpoints rejecting invocation due to transient unavailability or payload validation errors. This ticket defines acceptance criteria for a lightweight arbitration protocol that governs fragment commit, tool-decline semantics, and observable retry/fallback behaviors so product and infra teams can implement a robust, testable contract.
scope: Define API-level semantics (response envelope fields and status codes) and operator playbook. Includes: schema additions for fragment metadata, decline/soft-fallback codes for tool invocations, streaming checkpoint semantics, telemetry events, and a test matrix for e2e verification across hosted and dedicated deployments. Implementation work (runtime changes, SDKs, console surface) will be separate child issues.
out_of_scope: Runtime kernel optimizations, GPU scheduling, and dedicated autopilot scaling policies. Detailed SDK ergonomics are out of scope for this ticket; we only define wire-level semantics and acceptance tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Envelope extension: Every streamed structured fragment must include top-level metadata: fragment_id (UUID), seq (integer), committed (boolean), commit_token (string|null), and schema_version (semver string). Server and SDKs must accept and forward these fields without mutation.

2) Checkpoint semantics: A fragment may be emitted with committed=false; at most 30s after the final fragment for a logical object the server must emit a committed=true frame with the same fragment_id and a non-empty commit_token. Consumers must be able to reconcile partial state using fragment_id + seq.

3) Idempotency: commit_token acts as an idempotency key for the consumer and for tool invoke retries. If a tool receives a duplicate commit_token for the same fragment_id, the tool must treat it as a no-op (ack) and return HTTP 200 / accepted semantics to the Redwood gateway.

4) Tool-decline protocol: When an invocation to a tool fails due to transient capacity (e.g., 429 or 503), Redwood must emit a tool_status frame in-stream with fields: tool_name, tool_status: 'declined_transient', backoff_hint_ms (int), and suggested_fallback_model (string|null). The stream must continue to emit partial fragments where possible and mark affected fragments with committed=false.

5) Permanent tool errors: For schema/validation errors (400-range) returned by the tool, Redwood must emit tool_status with tool_status: 'declined_permanent', include error_class and error_snippet (first 256 chars), and attach a remediation_hint (string). The system must not retry automatically for declined_permanent unless explicitly requested by operator action.

6) Soft-fallback behavior: If a tool is declined_transient, early-stage consumers must accept a server-side fallback path: Redwood may (configurable) retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff and/or route to a fallback tool/model. Each retry attempt must be logged and emitted as an in-stream tool_attempt event with attempt_number and outcome.

7) Backpressure and flow control: If downstream consumers cannot keep up (consumer-side backpressure), the server must emit a stream-level flow_control frame with rate_limit_tokens (int) and expected_resume_eta_ms. The client SDK must expose a backpressure hook in the streaming API to surface this event.

8) Observability: Every tool_status, tool_attempt, and commit event must generate non-sampled telemetry with the following tags: fragment_id, tenant_id, route, model, tool_name, and outcome. These events must be queryable in Console within 2 minutes of occurrence (dashboard link in links).

9) Tests: Provide an automated test matrix in CI that covers: (a) partial fragments + eventual commit within 30s, (b) duplicate commit_token dedup behavior, (c) transient decline -> retry -> success, (d) permanent decline -> no-autoretry, (e) backpressure frame generation and SDK hook firing, (f) expiry of uncommitted fragments older than 5 minutes should trigger an expired fragment telemetry event and an operator alert rule.

10) Contract stability: schema_version increments must preserve read-compatibility for one minor version; any breaking change requires a rollout plan and a compatibility flag negotiated via the route config.

11) Documentation & operator playbook: Console must include a one-page playbook for incident responders that lists signals (metrics + traces), steps for manual tool re-routing, and recommended rollback procedures. Draft must be linked in links and approved by SRE and Support before release.

12) Privacy & Data Handling: Tool_status frames must not include full PII payloads. error_snippet must be sanitized (max 256 chars) and scrub any tokens or email-like patterns; validation must be validated by security review prior to GA.

13) Rollout gating: Feature must be behind a per-tenant toggle. Toggle defaults off. Beta tenants must be explicitly added via onboarding flow. Metrics for gating: increased error rate on function-calls, percent of fragments committed within 30s, and mean time to fallback. Release can proceed from beta to GA only when all gating metrics are within SLO thresholds for 14 days.

14) Backwards compatibility: For clients that do not parse new envelope fields, streams must fall back to legacy behavior: upstream continues to stream plain JSON but Redwood will emit a separate non-streamed commit webhook to ensure downstream systems can still observe commit events. This must be documented and included in migration notes.
test_plan: Unit tests for serializer/deserializer that include fragment metadata and commit frames.
Integration test harness simulating: tool unavailability (503/429), schema validation rejections (400-range), and duplicated commit_token flows.
End-to-end test using dedicated stack: produce 1k streamed fragments across varying sizes, assert >99% commit within 30s under nominal load.
Chaos test: inject 10% transient tool failures and verify fallback path triggers and telemetry surfaces retry attempts.
SDK test: verify backpressure hook is invoked when flow_control frames are emitted.
Security test: automated scrubbing checks on error_snippet to ensure no PII patterns remain.
Manual QA: walkthrough with Solutions Engineering using a third-party tool simulator; record runbook and edge-case notes.
Performance regression: measure 95th percentile end-to-end latency for commit frame emission and ensure < 50ms added overhead for streams that include fragment metadata.
scope_changes: 2025-02-20: Narrowed to wire-level contract + tests only (removed full SDK ergonomics). Rationale: decouple from SDK release cadence. Approver: Jordan Lee (PM).
2025-02-25: Added explicit commit_token idempotency requirement after infra review revealed duplicate delivery in some canary regions. Approver: Lina Morales (Infra).
open_questions: Q1: Should commit_token be globally unique per tenant or per route? (proposal: per-tenant)
Q2: What is the maximum permitted size for backoff_hint_ms? (proposal: cap at 120000 ms)
Q3: Should middleware that rewrites payloads be allowed to strip fragment metadata? (proposal: no, must be preserved)
review_notes: 2025-02-21 - SRE review: requested explicit metric names for failure signals (slo.fragment.commit_latency_seconds, slo.tool.decline_rate).
2025-02-26 - Security review: edge-case where error_snippet could leak tokens; added sanitization requirement and manual approval before GA.
2025-03-02 - UX review: suggested adding a small overlay in Console that surfaces live tool_status events for beta tenants. UX owner: Mei Chen.
implementation_notes: Map fragment_id to internal stream session on ingress to simplify dedup checks.
Tool gateway must return structured decline payloads (code, class, hint) to avoid string parsing in runtime.
Expose a per-route config: {fallback_enabled, max_retries, retry_policy, backoff_base_ms, allow_fallback_model}. Implementation teams to agree on config schema.
